title: Bridge treated every localhost port as a creel origin
description: CREEL_ORIGINS matched /^https?:\/\/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)[:/]/ — port-blind. Two consequences: (1) any page served on any localhost port could command the bridge, since Chrome match patterns cannot express a port and the connector is therefore injected into all of them; (2) the bridge refused to drive the user's own dev server on :3000, reporting it as a creel origin. Found by the real-browser end-to-end test, which serves creel and a fixture site on two random 127.0.0.1 ports.
close_reason: Origin checks are now exact-origin including port, from a configurable list (chrome.storage.local 'creelOrigins'); default is the Pages deployment plus localhost:8420 and 127.0.0.1:8420 (what 'just serve' uses). The Pages origin stays additionally path-scoped so another project on scbrown.github.io is not creel. Documented in extension/README.md as the supported way to run creel on a different port, since match patterns cannot express one. test-bridge-browser.js asserts all four cases.

title: Credentials must be writable by agents but never readable
close_reason: Flipped from blanket refusal to a write/read asymmetry, which is what the operator handing over a key actually needs. ui_fill now writes credential fields and reports only a character count; new ui_set_credential persists a provider API key directly. Every read path masks: ui_snapshot marks fields write-only, ui_text and ui_describe never carry values (hasKey stays a boolean). Detection is structural (input[type=password] plus name/id/placeholder/aria-label). A browser test writes three distinct secrets then asserts no ui tool anywhere echoes them, locally or across tabs.

title: Bridge hello is lost: connector announces at document_start, page listener loads last
description: extension/creel-connector.js posts creel-bridge:hello at document_start; app/browser-backend.js (script tag at onepagent.html:18829) installs its message listener only after the whole 18k-line document parses. The hello is a one-shot into the void, so bridge.present stays false and the full browser_* toolset never appears — the extension is effectively dead on arrival. Fix with a ping/hello handshake plus re-announce on DOMContentLoaded/load.
close_reason: Fixed: the page now PINGs on a short backoff and the connector answers with a hello (plus unprompted announcements at document_start/DOMContentLoaded/load as advisory). tests/test-bridge.js drives the hostile order — connector announcing into an empty window before browser-backend.js loads — and asserts discovery still succeeds.

title: Per-agent OPFS work dirs with git merge at burst end
description: VISION v1's merge discipline: each spawned agent gets an isolated workspace (per-agent OPFS dir or VFS namespace), works on a branch, and the dashboard merges results at burst end (isomorphic-git or the github-backend Git Data API path). Today agents share nothing and fleet_report carries prose only — parallel file edits from two agents cannot be reconciled.
acceptance_criteria: Burst of 2 agents editing the same checkout produces two branches and a dashboard-side merge (or conflict report); nothing merges silently.
close_reason: Per-tab sessionStorage checkout isolation (token stays shared); branch-per-agent convention in spawn briefing; github_merge integrates heads via GitHub merges API with explicit conflict reporting (never force-merges), auto-creating the base; github_branches for discovery. Verified: isolation across two tabs, and clean/uptodate/conflict merge paths.

title: Fleet shares one brain: quipu in a SharedWorker
description: Agent tabs currently fall back to in-memory quipu because the opfs-sahpool VFS is single-owner (first tab wins). Host the quipu-wasm store in a SharedWorker instead of a per-tab dedicated Worker so every same-origin tab talks to ONE store over ports — dashboard writes an episode, spawned agents query it instantly. Fallback to the dedicated worker where SharedWorker is unavailable (Chrome for Android). This is the enabler for VISION v2 'grounded cheap agents' inside a burst.
acceptance_criteria: Two tabs: episode written in tab A is quipu_query-visible in tab B without reload; OPFS persistence retained; single-tab behavior unchanged on browsers without SharedWorker.
close_reason: Leader-elected shared store: Web Locks pick a host tab whose dedicated worker owns OPFS; other tabs RPC over BroadcastChannel; takeover on leader death re-opens the same bytes. Verified: A→B and B→A visibility without reload, and data survival across leader death.

title: End-to-end extension test in real Chromium under a strict CSP
close_reason: test-bridge-browser.js loads the real extension into headless Chromium (--load-extension), serves creel and a fixture site on two different 127.0.0.1 ports, and drives the fixture end to end. The fixture sets script-src 'self' deliberately: an eval-based locator install passes every other test and fails only there. 13 assertions covering worker startup, the ping handshake, the port-aware origin gate, role/name driving, ref stability, auto-waiting, and a password that is written but unreadable.

title: Extension speaks the locator vocabulary for cross-origin tabs
close_reason: background.js injects app/creel-locator.js into the target tab as a FILE (never evaluated source — the MAIN world inherits page CSP) and dispatches locator ops through one self-contained function selected by name. browser_click/fill/type/press/hover/check/select_option/wait_for/text/snapshot now take the same locator shape as the ui_ tools; browser-backend.js lifts flat locator fields into the wire format. just check fails if the two copies of the engine drift; just sync-locator re-copies.

title: Playwright-shaped locator engine for the ui tools
close_reason: app/creel-locator.js: roles, accessible names, refs, strict resolution, auto-waiting. Locators are plain JSON so they cross the BroadcastChannel intact: {ref}, {role,name}, {text}, {label}, {placeholder}, {testId}, {selector}, plus exact/nth/timeout. ui_click/fill/type/press/hover/check/select_option/wait_for/text all auto-wait for visible+enabled first; ambiguity is an error listing candidates rather than a coin flip; ui_snapshot emits an indented aria tree with [ref] handles.

title: Real-browser UI tests over CDP, zero dependencies
close_reason: tests/browser.js drives real headless Chromium over CDP using Node 22's built-in WebSocket — no Playwright install, no node_modules, keeping the repo's zero-dependency property. Serves app/ over http because BroadcastChannel/Web Locks/sessionStorage need a real origin. test-ui-browser.js: 29 assertions against the actual 18k-line page, two real tabs, driven only through the ui MCP surface. Skips cleanly (exit 0) where no Chromium exists.

title: ARIA labels: every creel control has an accessible name
close_reason: Evidence-driven, not guesswork: snapshotted the real page in headless Chromium, found 1 nameless control and ~10 named only by glyph ('‹', '▶', '⧉') or by their own option list. Added aria-label to the panel toggles, send button (kept in sync with its Send/Stop/Guide state in updateButtons), system prompt editor, chat input, swarm role rows (per-role names, so 4 identical checkboxes became distinct), creel's own graph/fleet buttons, and all 17 selects. accessibleName now excludes content for form controls, per ARIA — a <select> is not named by its options. test-ui-browser.js asserts zero nameless controls, so a new unlabelled control fails CI.

title: The ui server is tab-local: an agent cannot operate another creel tab
description: creel-self.js ui_* tools only touch the calling tab's own DOM. An agent should be able to do for other bobbins what a user can: list creel tabs, describe/reconfigure them, snapshot their controls, read their transcript, type into their chat, stop their run. Needs a creel-ui BroadcastChannel RPC and an optional tab arg on every ui tool.
close_reason: Every ui_ tool now takes an optional tab (tab id / agent id / fleet label / 'root'), routed over a creel-ui BroadcastChannel and executed against the target tab's own DOM. New: ui_tabs, ui_snapshot, ui_transcript, ui_prompt, ui_stop. Two deliberate refusals: no agent fills a credential field (local or remote), and no tab prompts itself. 16 assertions in tests/test-ui-crosstab.js boot two tabs in one process.

title: Bridge op set is too thin for real web interaction
description: Only list_tabs/open_tab/navigate/read/query/click/fill. Missing: close_tab, wait_for, press (Enter/keys), select_option, scroll, history back/forward/reload, and a structured snapshot of interactive elements with stable selectors so agents stop guessing CSS.
close_reason: Bridge v0.2.0 adds close_tab, history (back/forward/reload), snapshot (every visible control with a uniqueness-verified selector), select_option, press, scroll, wait_for; read gained a limit, fill gained submit + prototype-setter writes so React sees the change. __ops advertises the surface so the page negotiates tools instead of failing mid-task. Injected code avoids eval (MAIN world inherits page CSP).

title: Harness PythonExec loads Pyodide from cdn.jsdelivr.net only — blocked on CN networks; app-side loader already fixed
description: The operator harness's PythonExec tool boots Pyodide from a hardcoded cdn.jsdelivr.net indexURL. On networks where jsDelivr is slow/blocked (live on 2026-08-14, mainland-China link): every PythonExec call times out at 120s ('Pyodide runtime download timed out... Try JSExec or a different approach'), which also disables the Pyodide-native tools (VfsToPyodide/PyodideToVfs) and workspace_cli. JSExec and NodeExec are unaffected (separate runtimes, no CDN). The creel app had the identical failure and the fix is ALREADY SHIPPED in app/onepagent.html (commit 99836bc): PYODIDE_CDN_HOSTS multi-CDN fallback — npmmirror first (https://registry.npmmirror.com/pyodide/<ver>/files/, note: root path, NOT /full/), then cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v<ver>/full/, fastly.jsdelivr.net, gcore.jsdelivr.net; 30s loader timeout per host, 120s runtime timeout, CORS-agnostic <script> injection (npmmirror omits CORS headers), Pyodide v314.0.3, no static loader tag. The harness Python tool needs the same treatment.
acceptance_criteria: PythonExec boots on CN-blocked networks: either (a) harness Pyodide loader gains the same multi-CDN fallback (npmmirror-first, 30s/120s timeouts, script-injection fallback) — copy PYODIDE_CDN_HOSTS + ensurePyodideLoaders() from app/onepagent.html — or (b) a CDN override env/config is exposed; or (c) an explicit documented decision to stay JSExec-first on such networks. Until then the interim workflow is: Python-flavored file ops via JSExec (vfsRead/vfsWrite), binary via vfsReadBinary/vfsWriteBinary.
notes: Verified 2026-08-17: creel's own side is complete, no remaining gap in this repo. app/onepagent.html has exactly ONE Pyodide load path (PYODIDE_CDN_HOSTS + ensurePyodideLoaders, ~6285-6365: npmmirror-first, 30s loader / 120s runtime timeouts, script-injection fallback); grep for indexURL finds no other hardcoded CDN. The remaining work is acceptance option (a) in the OPERATOR harness, which is not this repo — leaving open as a cross-repo tracking note, since nothing in creel can satisfy it.
close_reason: Moot: creel-yon disables the Python runtime by default, so the harness makes no Pyodide CDN request at all. The app-side multi-host loader remains behind the flag for whoever turns it back on.

title: Compile yupana to wasm for in-page structural analysis in creel
description: Bring yupana (live per-tenant code structure — call graph, refs, dataflow, impact) into creel as a fourth in-page knowledge source alongside quipu, so agents get 'what calls this / what will this break' on the VFS/checkout with zero network. Follows quipu's wasm playbook exactly (docs/design/wasm-support.md in quipu): (1) feature-gate the native stack off default — tokio 'full', clap, axum/rmcp (mcp feature), daemon/watch/git shell-outs — behind cfg(not(target_arch=wasm32)); (2) tree-sitter is the hard blocker: it compiles C grammars via cc, no libc on wasm32 — swap to web-tree-sitter (wasm grammars loaded at runtime) or tree-sitter's own wasm build, OR ship a wasm-bindgen dispatch that calls web-tree-sitter from JS and keeps only the graph/query layer in Rust; (3) getrandom wasm_js backend + RUSTFLAGS; (4) a creel-quipu-provider-style crate (wasm/yupana-provider) exposing analyze(files) + the yupana_* tool surface via wasm-bindgen, hosted in a worker like quipu; (5) feed it the FILES panel / github-checkout tree. Coordinate with whoever owns yupana's roadmap — the native-side feature-gating belongs in yupana proper (mirrors quipu-gsg/quipu-as2), the provider crate lives in creel.
acceptance_criteria: yupana lib compiles for wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features; a creel worker exposes yupana_analyze + refs/impact over the inpage MCP transport against VFS files; graph explorer or a tool shows call-graph facts; degrades gracefully when the bundle is absent (like quipu-wasm).

title: Code execution on the Pages origin: COI headers or Vivari
description: NodeExec (WebContainer) needs SharedArrayBuffer, which needs cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP) — GitHub Pages sets neither, so on the deployed origin only Pyodide runs. Options per VISION constraints: (a) coi-serviceworker shim (works on Pages, but breaks cross-origin fetches lacking CORP — audit DeepSeek/OpenRouter calls first), (b) swap WebContainer for Vivari (MIT, no COI requirement claim to verify, removes the commercial-license question), (c) accept Python-first and document it. Decide and implement.
acceptance_criteria: Either NodeExec boots on the deployed Pages site with LLM calls still working, or the README states Python-first with the reasoning.

title: The measurement: grounded vs ungrounded cheap agents
description: The bet VISION v2 stands on, still unmeasured: task success rate and cost-per-completed-task of small-model agents (deepseek-v4-flash) with vs without quipu grounding, vs one frontier agent. Design a small task suite that needs prior knowledge (seed the graph first), run bursts each way, capture tokens+outcomes via fleet_report, and write the numbers into docs/. The fleet + comms + shared-brain machinery makes this runnable now.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible bench doc with success-rate and cost columns for grounded/ungrounded/frontier; conclusions folded back into VISION.

title: Knowledge pack loader: fetch a distilled .db at session start
description: VISION v2: 'the graph snapshot ships to the browser read-only (fetched at session start)'. quipu-wasm can already open_from_bytes and CreelQuipu.importDb exists, but there is no fetch-a-pack flow: a configurable pack URL (or file picker) loaded at boot, shown in quipu_wasm_status, with the open question from VISION (whole pack vs topic-windowed via one server-side search) recorded as a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Setting a pack URL loads it at boot into the store (or a named graph); status reports pack provenance; works on the Pages deploy.

title: Work-queue leasing: N tasks, M agents, drain and requeue
description: VISION v1 burst controls. Today fleet_spawn is 1 task = 1 tab at spawn time. Add a task queue agents lease from via Web Locks (the lock auto-release on tab death requeues the task), fleet_drain (agents finish current task then stop claiming), and spawn-N-workers-against-queue. The leasing primitive is the piece that makes tab death recoverable instead of just visible.
acceptance_criteria: Queue of 5 tasks, 2 agent tabs: all 5 complete; killing a tab mid-task requeues it; fleet_drain stops claiming without killing work in flight.
close_reason: fleet_enqueue/spawn_workers/drain with Web Lock leasing; death-requeue and non-reentrant claiming verified across real tabs (4 tasks / 2 workers, kill mid-task recovered).

title: World model bumped to v2 — stores seeded at v1 will not re-seed
description: creel-self.js seeds the world model only when the version marker is absent, and the marker moved from creel-world-model-v1 to v2 to cover the cross-tab ui hands and the browser hands. A store that already holds v1 gets the v2 episode on next root election (different marker), so both versions coexist in the graph and quipu_cord on the old name still resolves. Decide whether old versions should be retired or kept as history — relates to creel-fxd (camayoc ontology alignment).
close_reason: Seeding now declares what it supersedes instead of leaving old versions unlinked. The graph stays append-only (facts true at write time — old versions are not rewritten): the new episode names the versions it supersedes, emits a node for each marked 'superseded by <current>; do not read as current', and a supersedes edge from current to each. An agent that lands on v1 via quipu_cord can follow supersedes forward to the newest. Verified against a real store in the browser test.

title: Agents are blind: no screenshot path because tool results are text-only
description: browser_snapshot gives structure, not pixels — a page whose meaning is in its layout is opaque to an agent. chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab would produce a data URL, but the vendored OnePagent harness renders tool results as text, so an image content block has nowhere to land. Needs a harness change (image content blocks in tool results) before a browser_screenshot op is worth adding. See docs/hands.md 'What is still missing'.

title: Align the creel world model with camayoc ontology discipline
description: creel-world-model-v1 mints ad-hoc types (Role, Subsystem, Surface, ToolServer) straight into the shared store. Camayoc owns what facts MEAN for the stack: competency questions before classes, reuse before minting (aegis:/prov:/quipu: first), rdfs:range not rdfs:domain. Write the competency questions the world model answers ('who dispatches?', 'what tools serve the root pane?', 'what conventions bind a bobbin?'), align/rename terms to stack vocabularies, and bump to creel-world-model-v2 with a migration note. The versioned marker node makes the re-seed safe.
acceptance_criteria: Competency questions documented; v2 model uses reused vocabulary where it exists; agents' quipu_cord entrypoint unchanged.

title: Ask for durable storage: navigator.storage.persist()
description: OPFS is evictable under storage pressure (VISION constraint 5). Request persistence at boot (navigator.storage.persist()), surface granted/denied + usage/quota in quipu_wasm_status, and nudge toward quipu_export_db / git push when denied.
acceptance_criteria: Status reports persistence state and quota; request made once, not nagged.
close_reason: navigator.storage.persist() requested once at bind; persisted/usage/quota surfaced in quipu_wasm_status with export nudge when evictable.

title: Background-tab throttling: measure and mitigate for agent tabs
description: VISION constraint 4: unfocused tabs get CPU-throttled; await-fetch LLM loops mostly survive but Pyodide/tool work may crawl. Measure a background agent tab's wall-clock vs focused, document findings, and if needed move tool execution into Workers (unthrottled) or recommend tiled windows / separate profile in the README. LIVE FINDING (creel-sbx run, 2026-08-14): on Android, navigating away from the browser suspends the tab entirely — network connections die and timers throttle, so worker leases wedge mid-task: tabs stay 'alive' at the Web Lock level but never progress, produce no episodes, and ignore fleet_send messages. Observed 4 leases wedged 16+ min with zero progress; recovery required aborting the worker tabs + re-enqueueing the leases (death-requeue did NOT fire for aborted workers). WEDGE RECURRED in the same run's second wave: all 3 fresh workers suspended again — the t4 worker ignored a direct fleet_send nudge for 5+ min, and two idle workers stopped claiming queued leases entirely (a queued t6 sat unclaimed 13 min next to idle workers). Recovery again = abort workers + abort ghost leases + re-enqueue + respawn fresh workers; with the tab kept visible the same two tasks (t4 transitive impact set, t6 ledger owner) completed in ~2 min — direct confirmation of suspend-on-hide. Also: tokenStart baselines can capture a stale (0) counter when the snapshot races the conversation-state flush, inflating input-token deltas. And: exact-grade normalization preserved '-' while collapsing all other punctuation, so 'Core team' failed against key 'Core-team'; norm() now maps '-' to space (fix applied uniformly to all arms).
acceptance_criteria: Measured numbers in docs; mitigation implemented or explicitly ruled unnecessary. Recommended mitigations: (1) stale-lease timeout — auto-requeue any lease running >N min without a report (would have self-recovered this run); (2) visibilitychange handler to checkpoint on hide / resume on visible; (3) README note 'keep the tab visible during bursts'; (4) flush token counters before baseline snapshot.

title: The weft: burst synthesis view and one-click write-back
description: VISION v3: at burst end, a synthesis pass runs across the parallel threads — dashboard view comparing fleet_report results (and diffs once per-agent branches exist), a synthesize action that hands all results to the operator's agent for a combined answer, and one-click write-back of what the burst learned into the quipu graph (episodes tagged with burst id).
acceptance_criteria: After a 3-agent burst: one dashboard view shows all results side by side, 'synthesize' produces a combined summary in the operator conversation, 'write back' lands tagged episodes in the store.
close_reason: fleet_synthesize collects finished results; dashboard Synthesize injects them into the operator conversation; fleet_writeback records takeaways as Burst-tagged quipu episodes. Verified: synthesis payload, writeback queryable in graph, dashboard control renders.

title: Bead-compatible issue API for use inside the harness
description: The repo tracks work with beads (bd), but the CLI is not available inside creel's browser harness — issues are reachable only as .beads/issues.jsonl, a passive export. Build a beads-compatible surface so operators and agents can read, create, claim, update and close issues with the same semantics (ids creel-XXX, statuses open/in_progress/closed, priorities, audit interactions) without the Dolt DB. Deliverables: (a) app/beads-store.js — shared store module (browser + Node) that parses/serializes the beads JSONL wire format and logs field_change interactions; (b) app/beads-backend.js — an in-page MCP server 'bd' (tools bd_ready / bd_list / bd_show / bd_create / bd_update / bd_close) reading and writing .beads/ through the harness VFS, with a localStorage fallback when no repo checkout is present; (c) tools/bd.js — a zero-dependency Node CLI running the same store against a real .beads dir, so sandboxes and shells can drive the tracker; (d) tests. The file format stays byte-compatible with beads' JSONL export so bd dolt push/pull remains the sync path. Where applicable, mirror issue state into the quipu graph (see creel-qup).
acceptance_criteria: bd_ready lists open issues by priority; bd_create appends a valid issue record and a field_change interaction; bd_update/bd_claim/bd_close transition status and append interactions; tools/bd.js performs the same ops on a real .beads directory; node tools/bd.js ready works; just check and unit tests green.

title: Theme: Intel One Mono typeface + Dracula palette
description: Restyle the harness with the Dracula color palette and Intel One Mono (OFL 1.1 licensed) as the primary UI/code font. The app must stay fully static/offline — no CDN — so the font is vendored into app/fonts/ with its license file, and the CSS variable set in onepagent.html moves to a dracula palette (backgrounds, foreground, accents, selection). Apply consistently to: the main shell, highlight.js token colors, the quipu explorer overlay, the fleet dashboard, and the MCP server list. Preserve contrast so snapshot/locator work stays legible, and keep the orange (agent) vs cyan (human) hand-highlight rings distinct on the new palette.
acceptance_criteria: CSS variables define the full dracula palette; @font-face serves Intel One Mono locally with LICENSE included; highlight.js tokens restyled to dracula; visual check shows a consistent theme across main/explorer/fleet surfaces; just test stays green.

title: System prompt: too large and stale — trim and document the full creel surface
description: DEFAULT_SYSTEM (~90 lines of sandbox prose) plus the volatile block (skills, media, pyodide, plan, sandbox, memory, time) is heavy, and neither mentions most creel capabilities: fleet tools (fleet_*), the browser bridge (browser_*), the github backend, measurement/bench, the quipu explorer, the ui hands (ui_*), per-agent workspaces, or the bd server once built. Agents discover capabilities late or never. Trim the stable prompt to essentials and reference a capabilities index instead of inline prose; name every in-page MCP server and tool family exactly; keep sandbox-specific guidance (PythonExec/JSExec/NodeExec vs Daytona) since it changes execution semantics; cut anything an agent can learn from tool schemas. The capabilities index should live in the quipu world model (see creel-qup) with docs/hands.md as the human-readable mirror.
acceptance_criteria: DEFAULT_SYSTEM measurably smaller (word count vs 2026-08-17 baseline); every creel MCP server and tool family named (ui_*, fleet_*, browser_*, github_*, bench_*, quipu_*, bd_*); volatile prompt pieces justified or removed; no capability regressions; tests green.
close_reason: Superseded by creel-l3k, which did the trim this bead asked for and then some: the prompt is 500 words, describes the current surface (state_*, durability, credentials), and a test now holds it to a word ceiling so it cannot drift back.

title: Bridge v-next: extend cross-origin capabilities
description: docs/hands.md 'What is still missing': no vision (blocked by creel-hty — tool results are text-only), no drag, no file pickers, no iframe traversal; ui_snapshot does not cross shadow roots. Scope the next extension milestone: (a) file inputs — set input[type=file] via DataTransfer from the injected locator engine; (b) iframe traversal — browser_snapshot/browser_* locators resolve into same-origin iframes; (c) shadow-root piercing in the locator's snapshot walker; (d) a permissions surface in the extension popup (view/edit creelOrigins). The bridge must keep refusing creel origins and keep exact-origin gating. Land each piece behind the existing tests/fixture, and document in extension/README.md + docs/hands.md.
acceptance_criteria: browser_snapshot sees into same-origin iframes and open shadow roots; an agent can attach a file to a fixture input[type=file] through the tool surface; extension popup shows and edits creelOrigins; bridge still refuses all creel origins; all browser tests green.

title: Accessible-name coverage: every control named, every control drivable, Playwright-shaped
description: creel-p8b added the test that no control is nameless; push to full parity: (a) audit every interactive element in the harness — main chat surface, settings, swarm-role modal, MCP server rows, fleet dashboard, quipu explorer overlay — for accessible names and keyboard operability (role coverage: button, tab, dialog, combobox, textbox, checkbox, switch, menuitem, slider); (b) the locator engine must reach every control type via the Playwright vocabulary (role/name, label, placeholder, testId, text, ref) with exact/nth/timeout, and ambiguous locators must keep failing loudly; (c) ui_* and browser_* keep identical tool shapes and auto-wait semantics (hands.md parity). Where a control is reachable but unnamed, fix the markup (aria-label / aria-labelledby), not the locator.
acceptance_criteria: A ui_snapshot of every app surface contains zero unnamed interactive controls; every control type is exercised at least once by an automated test through the tool surface (not internals); ambiguous-locator and auto-wait tests still pass; docs/hands.md updated with the coverage table.

title: Quipu leverage: the graph as cross-cutting substrate
description: Cross-cutting principle (operator directive 2026-08-17): where applicable, creel surfaces should read and write the shared in-page quipu graph instead of ad-hoc state. Candidate integrations: (a) beads issues mirrored as episodes — issue → entity, status transitions as facts — so agents can query the tracker through quipu_search/quipu_cord (complements creel-bds); (b) the capabilities index as a graph, world-model v2, replacing inline system-prompt prose (complements creel-spc); (c) theme/prompt decisions recorded as episodes; burst synthesis already writes back (creel-31a). Implement (a) and (b); document the pattern in app/README.md so future surfaces default to the graph.
acceptance_criteria: bd issue state queryable via quipu tools (entity per issue, transitions as facts); the world-model episode references the capabilities index; app/README.md documents the graph-first pattern; nothing regresses in just test.

title: Notify pages when a new version is deployed to GitHub Pages; refresh to update
description: Pages serves a static bundle, so tabs that stay open keep running the old code after a deploy — nobody (operator or agent) learns an update exists. Add no-server update detection: (a) commit version.json to the site root with {version, commit, built_at}, generated by a justfile target and refreshed by .github/workflows/pages.yml on deploy; (b) the harness fetches version.json on boot and on an interval with cache-busting (no-store) — align the cadence with the throttled ticker (see creel-vkh) — and also on visibilitychange so a returning tab checks immediately; (c) when the fetched commit/built_at is newer than the bundle's own, show a non-intrusive dismissible banner labelled "A new version is available — refresh to update" (ARIA role=status, see creel-89q) with a refresh action (location.reload()); (d) expose current vs latest through an in-page tool (a creel_version_status tool on a small inpage backend, mirroring beads-backend.js) so the creel agent can report and trigger the update; (e) never auto-reload without consent — refresh is the only update path, driven by the user or the agent.
acceptance_criteria: version.json is part of the deployed bundle (Pages workflow refreshes it with commit+built_at); a stale tab detects a new version within ~1 minute of deploy (poll + visibilitychange); banner appears once per version, is dismissible, ARIA-labelled, and offers a refresh action; agent can query current vs latest via an in-page tool and can initiate the update; justfile target updates version.json; unit tests cover compare-and-notify logic.

title: Disable Python (Pyodide) in the harness
description: Pyodide is a 10-15MB CDN download that gates PythonExec, VfsToPyodide/PyodideToVfs and the binary-hydration bridge, and it drags a Code Sandbox settings block, i18n strings and a large slice of DEFAULT_SYSTEM along with it. Stiwi wants Python off for now. Gate the whole runtime behind a single flag defaulting to off: no loader injection, no PythonExec/Pyodide tools in the tool list, no Python prose in the system prompt, Python UI hidden. Keep the code path intact behind the flag so re-enabling is one setting, not an archaeology project.
acceptance_criteria: A single PYTHON_ENABLED flag (default false) gates the Pyodide loader, the PythonExec/VfsToPyodide/PyodideToVfs tools, the sandbox UI block and the system-prompt paragraph. With the flag off no Pyodide network request is made and no Python tool appears in the tool list. Flipping it to true restores the previous behaviour. just check and just test pass.
close_reason: CREEL_FEATURES.python (app/creel-features.js), default off, gates the tool list, executeTool dispatch, ensurePyodide, the UI visibility filter and the DEFAULT_SYSTEM paragraph. tests/test-features.js proves the model sees no Python tool, an invented call is refused without injecting the loader, and the hash override puts everything back.

title: State persistence: sync config, keys and the quipu db to a private GitHub repo
description: creel holds everything in localStorage/IndexedDB/OPFS, which the browser may evict and which never follows the operator to another machine. The v2 cloud-sync engine (manifest + content-addressed objects + blobs, AES-GCM encryption, hash dedup, incremental push/pull) already has the right shape; only its transport is S3/SigV4. Add a GitHub transport over the Contents/Git-Data API so state lives in a PRIVATE repo the operator owns, configurable per user (Stiwi's is scbrown/creel-state). Unlike the S3 path this one MAY carry API keys, because the destination is a private repo the operator controls and the passphrase envelope still applies -- but carrying keys must be an explicit opt-in, not the default. The quipu db (export_db bytes) syncs as a blob.
acceptance_criteria: A state repo is configurable in settings (owner/repo, branch, path prefix) and defaults to <login>/creel-state. Push writes manifest + objects + blobs into the repo; pull restores them. Keys sync only when the operator opts in AND a passphrase is set. The quipu db round-trips: export, push, wipe, pull, import gives back the same graph. Refuses to push to a public repo. Tests cover the transport and the refusal.
close_reason: app/state-backend.js adds a GitHub transport at a new seam (_syncBackend) in the existing v2 sync engine, so the state repo reuses the manifest/objects/blobs design rather than duplicating it. One push is one commit via the Git Data API. Repo must be private, re-checked every push. Keys sync only on explicit opt-in AND a passphrase; a pull never overwrites a local key. The quipu .db travels as a manifest-named blob and is restored through CreelQuipu.importDb. Configurable in Settings and via state_configure/state_push/state_pull/state_status. tests/test-state.js covers all of it against an in-memory git remote: 18 assertions.

title: Per-tab agent state: isolate each tab's slice and give it its own quipu subgraph
description: Today every tab shares one leader-elected quipu store (creel.db) and one localStorage config, so two agent tabs cannot hold divergent state and nothing a tab learns is attributable to it. Give each agent tab a durable identity, a state slice that persists across reloads and into the state repo, and its own quipu subgraph -- a named plane within the shared store rather than a separate db, so cross-agent queries still work while writes stay attributable.
acceptance_criteria: An agent tab has a stable id that survives reload. Its slice (conversation, checkout, provider selection, working set) persists per tab and syncs to the state repo under that id. quipu writes from a tab land in that tab's subgraph and are queryable both scoped and fleet-wide. Two tabs can hold divergent state without clobbering each other.
close_reason: Two mechanisms, deliberately different in strength. STATE: every tab has a stable slice id (fleet agent id if spawned, else the sessionStorage tab id); state_push/state_pull take scope: 'agent' and write under state/agents/<id>/, a sibling of the shared tree, so two tabs hold divergent state without clobbering each other or the operator's. GRAPH: all tabs keep sharing ONE quipu store — a fleet whose agents cannot see what each other learned is not worth running — and each tab stamps the episodes it ingests with group_id agent:<id>, so facts are scoped/reviewable/retractable per agent while reads stay fleet-wide. An explicit group_id from the caller always wins. 11 new assertions in tests/test-state.js, including that withScope does not leak and that reads are never silently scoped.

title: Modularize onepagent.html: extract the 16.7k-line inline script
description: app/onepagent.html is 18871 lines / 1.1MB, of which one inline <script> is 16706 lines. Nothing can be reviewed, diffed or reasoned about at that size, and every agent that reads it burns its context on the file. Extract along the banner-comment seams into ordered classic scripts in app/. Classic (not module) scripts share one global lexical environment, so top-level const/let stay visible across files and inline onclick= handlers keep working -- the extraction is mechanical and semantics-preserving as long as script order is kept and no function is split. Phase it: i18n, then styles, then each runtime section, verifying the browser tests after every phase.
acceptance_criteria: onepagent.html is under 2000 lines and contains markup plus ordered script tags. No extracted file exceeds 900 lines. just check parses every extracted file and just test (including the real-Chromium half) passes at every phase boundary.
close_reason: onepagent.html: 19134 -> 1523 lines. The 16932-line inline script is now 26 ordered classic scripts in app/harness/ (largest 1081; the two over 900 are one i18n object literal and a section with no top-level split point). The ~700-line inline stylesheet is app/harness.css. Extraction was verbatim and verified two ways: each part parses alone, and the parts concatenate back to the original byte for byte. just check now parses the remaining inline blocks and app/harness/*, and tools/check-shell.js fails the gate if a part is missing from the service worker's precache list or loaded out of order.

title: Interface: cut the sidebar to a calm default and hide the rest behind progressive disclosure
description: The left panel stacks ten always-present sections (conversations, system prompt, skills, swarms, files, tools, web search, todos, sub-agents, hooks, context) and settings is a wall of every knob the harness has. The operator sees the union of every feature at once instead of the few they use. Establish a default surface -- conversations, files, the chat -- and put the rest behind an explicit reveal, remembering what the operator opened. Advanced settings collapse by default. Nothing is deleted: this is disclosure, not removal, and every control keeps its accessible name so the ui_* tools still drive it.
acceptance_criteria: A first-run tab shows at most four sidebar sections. Every hidden section is reachable in one action and its open/closed state persists. Settings groups advanced knobs behind collapsed headings. Every control keeps a stable accessible name; the ui_* browser tests still find and drive the controls they drove before.
close_reason: Left panel: 11 always-present sections cut to 4 (conversations, files, tools, context). The other 7 carry data-tier=more and the hidden attribute — out of the layout AND the accessibility tree, so an agent's snapshot describes the panel the operator is actually looking at. A 'More sections' chip row lists every hidden one by its own label; one click reveals or re-hides, persisted in creel_panel_shown. Settings' ten groups are now native <details>, closed by default, remembered per group by i18n key. Nothing deleted, every control keeps its accessible name: tests/test-ui-browser.js now proves an agent reveals a section by clicking its chip by name, exactly as the operator does.

title: System prompt: rewrite for the surface creel actually has
description: DEFAULT_SYSTEM still opens on execution semantics for PythonExec / JSExec / NodeExec and a Daytona remote sandbox, which is the vendored OnePagent inheritance rather than what creel is. With Python disabled (creel-yon) most of that prose describes tools that no longer exist, and the newer surfaces -- the state repo, per-tab identity, the bd tracker, the measurement suite -- are named in one line or not at all. Rewrite it to describe the live surface, keep it short, and make the tool-family index the thing an agent can act on.
acceptance_criteria: DEFAULT_SYSTEM names only tool families that exist under the current flags, describes state persistence and per-tab identity, and stays at or below its current word count. No paragraph describes a disabled runtime. The world-model episode and docs/hands.md are updated to match.
close_reason: DEFAULT_SYSTEM rewritten: 500 words (was 508) while covering more surface. Opens on what running in a tab costs and buys rather than 'a browser-based virtual sandbox'. Names every live family including state_*, adds the durability rule (three doors: github_push, state_push, quipu) and the credential asymmetry, drops the per-family tool enumerations that duplicated the schema list. World model bumped to creel-world-model-v4 with durability and state-repo nodes and their edges; docs/hands.md and README updated to match. tests/test-features.js pins the families, the durability language and a word ceiling.

title: Split the oversized creel modules
description:
creel-fleet.js is 1122 lines and creel-self.js 805, both well past the point where a reader can hold them. Same disease as onepagent.html — but NOT the same cure. The harness split was mechanical because it was one flat script: classic scripts share a global lexical environment, so moving a line between files changed nothing. These two are IIFEs, so splitting them means restructuring a closure and re-exposing its internals through a namespace. That is a real refactor, not a move.

BLOCKED ON creel-psr. creel-fleet.js owns Web Locks leasing, crash detection, heartbeats and the cross-tab bus, and has no test of its own. Restructuring that with nothing to catch a regression risks a bug that only appears under real parallelism and reads as flakiness when it does. Write the fleet test first, then split.

creel-self.js is the safer half and could go first: its seams (locator bridge / tool surface / UI reach) are covered by test-ui-crosstab and test-ui-browser.
acceptance_criteria: No file in app/ exceeds 600 lines. just check and just test pass. The extension's copy of the locator engine still matches the app's byte for byte.

title: creel-state: scaffold the state repo layout
description: scbrown/creel-state is an empty private repo. It is the destination for creel-3ru, so its layout is a contract between the two: what a manifest is, where objects and blobs live, how a per-tab agent slice is addressed, what is encrypted and what is legible. Write that down in the repo itself so a human opening it can tell what they are looking at, and so a future creel can read a state repo it did not write.
acceptance_criteria: creel-state holds a README describing the layout and the encryption envelope, a versioned layout spec, and a .gitignore. The layout matches what creel-3ru actually writes.
close_reason: creel-state now holds README.md (what the repo is, key policy, how to restore, how to read a diff of content-addressed data), LAYOUT.md (version 2 spec: manifest authority, SHA-256 over plaintext, OPA1 envelope, $blob refs, agents/<id>/ addressing, and the invariants each side upholds) and a .gitignore. Pushed to claude/creel-state-persistence-h7x24k.

title: Beads store test asserts a stale priority rule
description: tests/test-beads.js asserts that create({priority: 1}) is rejected, but beads-store.js accepts 1..3 and the tracker already holds P1 issues (creel-9wn, creel-hkv, creel-89q). The test fails at the tip of main, so just test-unit is red before any new work starts and the gate cannot tell a real regression from this.
acceptance_criteria: The test asserts the rule the store actually enforces (0 and 4 rejected, 1..3 accepted). just test-unit is green on an otherwise unmodified tree.
close_reason: Test asserted P1 was invalid; the store accepts 1..3 and the tracker uses P1. Test now checks the real boundaries (0 and 4 rejected). Also fixed the title assertion, which passed a non-empty title while expecting a title error, and made bd.js take its id prefix from .beads/metadata.json instead of the checkout directory name so a clone named anything else keeps minting creel-xxx ids.

title: Fleet has no test of its own
description: app/creel-fleet.js is 1122 lines of the most concurrency-sensitive code in the repo — Web Locks leasing, crash detection by lock release, heartbeats, the BroadcastChannel bus, agent/worker tab boot — and nothing tests it directly. test-ui-crosstab covers the ui routing, test-device covers the caps, and the browser tests open agent tabs but assert about the UI rather than about leasing. This is why creel-hun (splitting the file) is blocked: restructuring a closure that owns leases and locks, with no test to catch a regression, risks a bug that only appears under real parallelism and looks like flakiness when it does.
acceptance_criteria: A test drives real leasing in real tabs: a task is claimed by exactly one tab, a tab that dies releases its lease and another claims it, a heartbeat gap is detected, and the work log records each transition. It fails if leasing lets two tabs claim one task.
